title: ‘Socheton’: A Culturally Appropriate AI Tool to Support Reproductive Well-being
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not use a formal benchmark to measure a model's performance. Instead, it conducts an ethnographic and user study to understand the impact of faith-based values and religious beliefs (primarily Islam) on the acceptance of reproductive well-being technologies in Bangladesh. The research measures the challenges and requirements for designing a culturally and religiously sensitive AI tool, focusing on aspects like appropriate language, combating misinformation that contradicts religious beliefs, and aligning with community values.
findings: Key findings indicate that reproductive healthcare initiatives in Bangladesh often fail due to clashes with the community's faith-based (predominantly Islamic) values. Modern healthcare concepts are frequently met with suspicion, perceived as conflicting with religious beliefs on topics like contraception and family size. The study found that religious sentiments heavily influence discussions on sensitive topics, as seen in the opposition to LGBTQ+ concepts in school curricula for being 'against Islam.' Participants suggested that for technology like the proposed 'Socheton' AI tool to be accepted, it must respect these values, use culturally and religiously appropriate language, and involve religious institutions like local mosques as stakeholders. The research highlights that religion can also be 'weaponized' in identity politics to control the discourse on reproductive awareness.
